text: Moss claims the north stone / patient where the sun won't reach / softness wins the war
Lightning splits the oak / for a moment the whole field / remembers its name
River finds the crack / no one taught it where to go / it simply went down
Snow erases roads / the hills forget their fences / briefly we are lost
Mushrooms after rain / the forest's quiet ledger / of who has rotted
Wind bends the tall grass / each blade pretends to follow / none of them agree
Tide pools hold the moon / in water no deeper than / a child's cupped two hands
Pine cones open slow / counting heat they cannot feel / fire writes their spring
A single red leaf / decides for the whole maple / autumn has begun
Fog drinks the mountain / by morning gives it all back / nothing was missing
Roots crack the boulder / a century of pressing / no hand ever pushed
Ice lets go the branch / one slow drop at a time learns / how to be a stream
Wildflowers in the ditch / no gardener chose this place / they bloomed anyway
Thunder counts the miles / between the flash and the fear / both arrive too late
Sand keeps the gull's track / until the next wave decides / it was never there
Subway doors closing / the man who almost made it / shrugs at his own life
Neon in the rain / the puddle holds a city / brighter than the real
Pigeons own the square / the statues only pretend / to be in charge here
Elevator hum / six strangers agree to look / only at the doors
Construction at dawn / the city builds itself up / on someone's lost sleep
Crosswalk countdown blinks / the whole crowd leans like one beast / waiting to be freed
Steam from the manhole / the street exhales what it ate / nobody looks down
Apartment windows / two hundred separate lives / share one wall of brick
Taxi in the rain / its yellow the only warmth / on the gray cold block
Graffiti painted / over by morning—someone / kept the photograph
Late bus never comes / the schedule a kind of myth / we agree to trust
Skyscraper at dusk / lights flick on floor after floor / someone's working late
Street musician plays / more to the coins than the crowd / both keep walking past
Fire escape garden / tomatoes against the rust / the city's small revolt
Rush hour swallows me / I am a current, not a man / the crowd does the steering
You took the window / I took the aisle—somehow / we still chose to share
Her hand finds my hand / in the dark without looking / we learned this by heart
We argue then sleep / the bed a country divided / dawn redraws the line
He laughs at my joke / one beat late—he was hearing / something else first
Two cups by the sink / one has lipstick, one does not / morning leaves its proof
The space on the couch / shaped exactly like the one / who used to sit there
We say goodnight twice / once for show, once because / neither wants to hang up
She keeps my old coat / says it still smells like the year / we had nothing else
Your name in my phone / still 'Do Not Answer'—I lied / I answer each time
We grew like two trees / planted close, roots now tangled / which leaf belongs where
He fixes the sink / it was never the sink, but / a way to keep staying
The fight was over / hours ago—still I rehearse / what I should have said
Old friends, longer pauses / the silence comfortable now / where words used to be
She left the light on / a small mercy for the one / coming home too late
We split the last bite / generous, then watch it go / into the wrong mouth
Grandmother's kitchen / I smell it in a stranger / passing on the street
The song from that year / plays in a store—I stand still / letting it find me
I forget your face / but not the way you tilted / it to hear me speak
Childhood house, smaller / when I drove past last winter / or maybe I just grew
A photo falls out / of the book—the summer when / we still believed it
The phone number stays / in my fingers though the line / has long since gone dead
I keep the broken / watch—it stopped at the one hour / I want to keep close
Dust on the piano / no one plays it now but I / still hear her practice
The smell of cut grass / and I am eight again, brief / before the blade stops
Letters in a box / her handwriting still leaning / forward, full of hope
I walk the old route / my feet remember the turns / my mind has let go
The taste brings it back / a whole decade folded in / one bite of plain bread
We were going to / I keep the half-made plans like / they might still come true
Mother's voice, saved / I never press play, just hold / the message to keep
The scar tells the day / better than I could—my skin / keeps the truer log
The kettle whistles / steam fogging the cold window / morning insists on
A button, missing / the coat still warm—we forgive / what we cannot fix
House keys on the hook / they have opened the same door / ten thousand evenings
The chipped favorite mug / I drink from the good side, turn / the flaw toward the wall
Pencil worn to stub / it wrote more than the long ones / sleeping in the cup
Umbrella inside / drying like a tired bat / it did its one job
The clock's second hand / sweeps over the same numbers / never once grown bored
Worn path in the rug / between the door and the chair / a life made visible
Spare button in the / drawer, waiting forty years / for a coat long gone
The lamp's pull-chain click / smaller than a heartbeat, ends / the whole day at once
Reading glasses lost / atop my own forehead—I / search the house for me
The doormat says WELCOME / faded now to ELCO—still / it means the same thing
Salt shaker, half full / it will outlive this dinner / the next, and us too
The cracked phone screen / a spiderweb spun across / your smiling, frozen face
Old wooden spoon, worn / thin on one side from stirring / one pot for years
His coat on the hook / I cannot bring myself to / move it to the box
The dog waits by the door / for the step that will not come / I wait beside him
Two plates, force of habit / I set the table for two / then sit with the one
Her garden still blooms / unaware the hand that planted / it has stopped its work
I dial then remember / the silence on the line is / all that answers now
We scatter the ash / the wind takes him faster than / I am ready for
His chair at the head / no one sits there—the empty / says more than a name
The voicemail's full now / I delete a stranger's call / to keep one more day
Spring comes regardless / cruel in its insistence that / the world keeps on green
I laugh, then feel guilt / as if joy were betrayal / of the one who's gone
The half-read novel / bookmarked where she stopped—I'll not / learn how it ends
Snow on the fresh grave / the world tucks him in gently / I stand in the cold
His handwriting on / the grocery list—milk, bread—I / buy them, bring them home
The phone lights—his name— / then I remember I kept / it to feel him close
Grief is a long tide / it goes out, I think I'm dry / then it comes back in
First light on the wall / I lie still, unwilling yet / to begin the day
Tea going cold while / I watch the steam give itself / up to the still room
The house breathes slowly / everyone asleep but me / and the humming fridge
Rain on the tin roof / I have nowhere to be—rare / permission to stay
Snow falls without sound / the world turns its volume down / I lower mine too
Bath water cooling / I stay past the point of warm / for the quiet alone
The cat on my chest / rising, falling with my breath / neither of us moves
Last page of the book / I close it slowly, hold off / the return to noise
Coffee before dawn / the only one awake, I / own the whole gray hour
Wind chimes, far away / I stop weeding just to hear / where the breeze has been
Candle nearly out / I let it choose its own end / rather than blow it
Empty afternoon / nothing happens—and that is / the whole gift of it
The pause after rain / before the birds resume their / argument with sky
I sit with the dusk / not reaching for the light switch / letting evening come
Stretching after sleep / one perfect yawn before the / day demands its due
The same commute again / I know each crack in the road / none of them know me
Inbox at zero / a victory that will last / exactly one breath
Coffee gone cold twice / reheated, drunk anyway / the meeting ran long
Badge swipes me through doors / the building knows my number / better than my name
Friday at five sharp / the parking lot empties like / a held breath let go
New guy asks for help / I remember being lost / I clear my whole day
Spreadsheet's final row / I tally a year of work / it fits on one screen
The boss says 'team' a lot / I notice it most the week / before the layoffs
Lunch at my desk again / the sandwich and the deadline / share the same small space
Retirement party / cake and a clock—they give him / time now that it's spent
The night shift hands off / to the morning—two tired / nods, the work goes on
Out of office set / I send it gladly, then check / my email anyway
Promotion came through / more money, longer hours / I gained and I lost
The tools hang in rows / each one shaped by the hand that / reached for it for years
Last one in the office / I turn off all the lights / the day finally mine
Bread rising slowly / I cannot rush the yeast—some / things take their own time
Grandmother's recipe / 'a pinch'—I never learned how / much her hand could hold
Soup on the back burner / the whole house smells of patience / and a long cold day
The first ripe tomato / warm from the vine, I eat it / there in the garden
We share one orange / passing segments back and forth / sweetness, then the pith
Burnt the rice again / the smell of my distraction / we eat it anyway
Cold pizza at dawn / the leftover of a night / that felt worth the keeping
Steam off the dumplings / we wait, then can't wait, and burn / our too-eager tongues
Salt on the melon / the strange wisdom of grandfathers / proven true at last
The last cookie sits / on the plate—politeness keeps / us all from the want
Coffee and the news / bitterness with bitterness / the morning's honest
Mother peels apples / one long unbroken ribbon / falls into the bowl
Wine breathes on the counter / opening slowly the way / good talk opens too
Eggs cracked in the hot pan / the small violence that begins / a gentle morning
We argue, then I cook / the chopping settles something / words could not put down
The hawk hangs unmoving / pinned to the wind it rides—still / and racing at once
Tide goes out for good / leaving the boats to lean on / mud they cannot sail
A single crow lands / on the wire—the whole gray sky / now has a sentence
Whale breaks the surface / a mountain that breathes, then choosing / the dark deep again
The moon over water / a road of light that always / points back to the watcher
Geese in a long V / pulling winter behind them / south, the way of old
Jellyfish drifting / no brain, no plan, no struggle / yet it goes somewhere
Stars I cannot name / shine indifferent to the lack / they were here before me
The old dog dreams—paws / twitch at a rabbit he caught / in a younger field
Lightning over sea / for one second the water / wears the whole sky's face
Sparrow in the eaves / building a home in the gap / our walls forgot to seal
The deep keeps its dead / its light, and its old monsters / we only borrow waves
Cat watches the bird / a hunger it will not feed / behind the cold glass
Comet won't return / for a lifetime of lifetimes / I look while I can
Fog over the bay / boats call out to each other / blind, but not alone
